Read-only configuration selecting whether the arm runs; it carries no per-process state, so it is carrier-wide by construction and cannot be a scope defect.

Host thread-local cell SYSTEM_CHARGE_WINDOW in crates/carrick-runtime/src/kernel/objects.rs holding this HOST thread's open system-CPU charge window for the logical guest thread its executor is currently running. It is per-host-thread by construction — the CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID reading it brackets describes this host thread and no other — and it selects no container state: the logical thread it charges is named by a WEAK reference that every use upgrades, so it neither keeps a retired Thread alive nor can be aliased by a recycled allocation, and the executor closes it at every boundary audit.

The guest CPU count the carrier's installed scheduling policy fixes, published once when the carrier builds its scheduler and read by every guest-visible CPU surface (nproc, sched_getaffinity, /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/stat, /sys/devices/system/cpu). It replaces the equally process-global host_facts::LOGICAL_CPUS OnceLock as that surface's authority rather than adding a second one; HVPatch runs one carrier per process, so one answer is the whole truth, and a second DIFFERENT publication aborts because nproc has already answered. It selects nothing container-owned and cannot overwrite container state.
